pages.text: You've taken 3/4 of an amount. Now take half of 3/4 of a square. The cuts make 8 equal pieces, and that half is 3 of them, so half of 3/4 is 3/8.

pages.name: Half of a quarter
pages.task: The bar shows 1/4 shaded. Colour half of the shaded quarter.
pages.why: Cut in half the long way, the bar has 8 equal pieces. Half of the quarter is one of them, so it is 1/8.

pages.text: [[Of]] means times, so half of 3/4 is 1/2 × 3/4. The 1 row of 3 taken gives the top, 1 × 3. The 2 rows of 4 give the bottom, 2 × 4.

pages.name: Two thirds of three quarters
pages.task: What is 2/3 × 3/4? Simplify it as far as it goes.
pages.why: The tops make 2 × 3 = 6 and the bottoms 3 × 4 = 12. 6/12 simplifies to 1/2, half the square.

pages.name: Half of three eighths
pages.why: The tops make 1 × 3 = 3 and the bottoms 2 × 8 = 16. Cut in half the long way, the bar has 16 equal pieces.

pages.alt: Three bars, one above another, each cut into 5 fifths. 3 lots of 2 fifths shaded, one lot to a bar, each labelled 2/5. Under them, 3 × 2/5 = (3 × 2)/5 = 6/5. 3 of the 3 fifths outside the first bar have moved up into it, so it is full, labelled 1, and one fifth is in the second, labelled 1/5. 6/5 = 1 and 1/5.

pages.text: 3 × 2/5 means three lots of 2/5. That makes 6 fifths, so only the top is multiplied. 6/5 is one whole and one fifth, 1 1/5.

pages.name: Four lots of three eighths
pages.why: Four lots of 3 eighths make 12 eighths, 12/8. Eight of them fill a whole, so it is 1 4/8, or 1 1/2.

pages.alt: A square with sides of 1 and 1/2: a whole 1 by 1 square, a strip of 1/2 down the right, a strip of 1/2 along the bottom and a corner. Half-lines cut it into 3 rows of 3 quarters, and under it, 3/2 × 3/2. 9 of the 9 quarters are shaded and counted. 3/2 × 3/2 = (3 × 3)/(2 × 2) = 9/4 = 2 and 1/4. The 4 quarters of the two strips, which multiplying only 1 × 1 and 1/2 × 1/2 misses, are highlighted.

pages.why: 1 1/2 is 3/2, and 2/3 × 3/2 = 6/6, which is 1. Two thirds of three halves is two halves.

pages.name: A reel of cable
pages.task: A reel of cable is 3/4 full. A job uses 1/3 of what is on it. What fraction of a full reel is that?
pages.why: Of means times, so the job uses 1/3 × 3/4 = 3/12 of a full reel. That simplifies to 1/4.

pages.name: Less than 5
pages.task: Which of these is less than 5?
pages.why: Multiplying by a fraction between 0 and 1 gives only part of a number. 2/3 is less than 1, so 5 × 2/3 = 10/3, or 3 1/3.

pages.name: Two mixed numbers
pages.why: 2 1/2 is 5/2 and 1 1/2 is 3/2, so the picture holds 5 × 3 = 15 quarters. 5/2 × 3/2 = 15/4, which is 3 3/4.
